newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tankers flat to weaker, quiet.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tankers flat to weaker, quiet.

text.p: Very large crude carriers (VLCCs) from the Middle East were flat to weaker amid low enquiry on Tuesday, brokers said.
Very few fresh fixtures were reported and one broker said South Korean and Japanese charterers appeared to be holding off in an attempt to push rates down further.
Mideast/Japan VLCCs were assessed at about W68 although no vessels were confirmed fixed on this route. This level is well down on the year high of W75 earlier this month.

West Africa/U.S. Gulf VLCCs were at a notional W65 in very quiet trade, while Suezmaxes (130,000 tonne vessels) were at a stable W87.5/90. The latter market was somewhat more active than VLCCs, with the 120,000 tonne Ephesos fixed at W87.5 Qua Iboe/USG for Mobil.
The cross-Med Suezmax was lacklustre, with owners seeking around W95/100 but brokers said they expected vessels to be fixed lower at around W90.
Inter-U.K./Cont 80,000 tonne vessels (Aframaxes) continued to be fixed at about W125 in one of the busier segments of the market, with a couple of 74,000/76,000 tonne Ventspils cargoes done at W145.
The Caribs/upcoast market was stable with 70,000 tonne crude cargoes still at W170 and 50,000 tonne fuel oil stems at W185. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
